# Incident Report: 2024-09-04 Traffic Analysis Exercise

## Victim host

| Field | Value | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| IPv4 | 172.17.0.99 | Consistent source of all suspicious flows; only non-infrastructure LAN host |
| MAC | 18:3d:a2:b6:8d:c4 | ARP table binds this MAC to 172.17.0.99 (and appears as `dhcp.hw.mac_addr` on the same host's DHCP request) |
| Hostname | DESKTOP-RNVO9AT (domain bepositive.com, AD domain controller WIN-CTL9XBQ9Y19 at 172.17.0.17) | DHCP option 12 hostname, NBNS `DESKTOP-RNVO9AT<00>/<20>`, DNS self-registration queries for `DESKTOP-RNVO9AT.bepositive.com` |
| Logged-in user | afletcher | Kerberos `CNameString` on AS-REQ/TGS traffic between 172.17.0.99 and the DC 172.17.0.17 |

## Malware family

**Attribution: behavioral, not signature-confirmed.** No IDS/Suricata alerts were provided with this capture, so the name below is inferred purely from traffic behavior, not a signature match.

The host runs a **pay-per-install-style loader/bot**. Behavioral signals:

- Beacons every ~70-90 seconds (48 check-ins across the capture) via HTTP POST to a bare IP (no DNS lookup ever precedes it) at `/foots.php`, sending small encrypted/binary blobs (`Content-Type: application/octet-stream`) and getting trivial `200 text/html` acks back.
- One `GET /index.php?id=&subid=qIOuKk7U` returned a pipe-delimited gate record: `HckDcK0czXjaq48jVHNn|qIOuKk7U|http://79.124.78.197/index.php|` — a bot-ID + affiliate/subid tracking tag + callback URL. This bot-ID/subid/gate-URL check-in structure is characteristic of pay-per-install loader infrastructure (PrivateLoader-style), used to install additional payloads for paying affiliates.
- The C2 IP is never resolved via DNS in this capture, consistent with a hardcoded C2 address baked into the loader.
- Roughly 2 seconds before the first `/foots.php` beacon, the host pulled ~701 KB over TLS from `www.bellantonicioccolato.it` (46.254.34.201:443) — a legitimate Italian bakery site, almost certainly compromised and used to stage the payload. This is the likely delivery vector, but the transfer is TLS-encrypted so the payload itself could not be recovered or hashed from this capture.
- The capture starts at host boot/logon and the beacon begins only 155 seconds in, meaning the initial infection/delivery event that planted the loader is not visible in this pcap — the capture picks up an already-established beacon.

No executable file was recoverable in the clear (HTTP object export yielded only tiny text artifacts — Adobe/Windows telemetry files, and the encrypted `foots.php`/`index.php` blobs), so **no file name or SHA256 hash can be reported** for the payload itself.

## Indicators of Compromise

| Type | Value | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| C2 endpoint | `79.124.78.197:80` | 48x HTTP POST beacons to `/foots.php` and gate exchange on `/index.php`, all bare-IP HTTP, no DNS lookup ever observed for this IP |
| URL | `http://79.124.78.197/foots.php` | Repeated POST, `application/octet-stream` bodies, from 172.17.0.99 |
| URL | `http://79.124.78.197/index.php?id=&subid=qIOuKk7U` | GET returning bot-ID/subid/gate-URL record |
| URL | `http://79.124.78.197/index.php` | Follow-up POST after gate check-in |
| Domain (delivery-stage host) | `www.bellantonicioccolato.it` (46.254.34.201) | TLS SNI in ClientHello, 701 KB downloaded over TLS 2 seconds before first C2 beacon; flagged as likely compromised legitimate site, not a registered malicious domain |

**Not IOCs (benign context):** `bepositive.com`/AD/Kerberos/LDAP/SMB traffic to 172.17.0.17 (domain controller, normal AD operation); all Microsoft telemetry, Office, Windows Update, MSN, Bing, WNS, NCSI endpoints; `acroipm2.adobe.com` (legitimate Adobe update-check telemetry); `x1.c.lencr.org` and the `ctldl.windowsupdate.com` CTL/CRL downloads (Windows CryptoAPI trust-list updates); `sso.godaddy.com` (background TLS handshake, no request content observed).

## Summary

DESKTOP-RNVO9AT (172.17.0.99, MAC 18:3d:a2:b6:8d:c4), logged in as user **afletcher** on the bepositive.com AD domain, is infected with a pay-per-install loader/bot. The loader most likely arrived via a payload staged on the compromised site `www.bellantonicioccolato.it`, then began beaconing every 70-90 seconds to hardcoded C2 `79.124.78.197` over plain HTTP (`/foots.php`, `/index.php`), performing a bot-ID/affiliate-subid gate check-in consistent with PPI loader infrastructure. Attribution to a specific named family is behavioral only; no signature or recoverable payload hash was available to confirm it.
